 Russell Brand’s jail hell revealed: Vermin-infested cells, violent inmates and drug searches 
 By 
 Nate Grant 
 Published 
 Nov. 6, 2026, 9:51 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Russell Brand is facing a grim reality behind bars at one of London’s most troubled prisons.
 The “Get Him to the Greek” actor, 51, is being held at HMP Wandsworth following his conviction for rape and three counts of sexual assault . Inside, he faces a facility plagued by overcrowding, vermin and violence, according to official watchdog reports.
 The Victorian prison is operating at 163% of its normal capacity, compared to a national average of 107%, according the Howard League for Penal Reform .
 Wandsworth has 1,457 inmates despite having certified normal accommodation for just 894.
 A 2024 report by Wandsworth’s Independent Monitoring Board painted an especially bleak picture of life behind bars, describing conditions inside as “inhumane” and warning of severe risks caused by overcrowding.

 The report stated that two men were routinely required to share single-occupancy cells, with some described as “cramped, squalid and featuring broken or missing windows, furniture and fittings.”
 Basic necessities were also in short supply, with inmates sometimes going two or three weeks without a full change of clothing. Showers were described as damp, unhygienic and insufficient in number, while poor ventilation allowed mold to return even after refurbishment.
 The report also found that crumbling floors provided access for vermin, heating was intermittent because of frequently malfunctioning boilers and summer cell temperatures frequently topped 95 degrees Fahrenheit.
 Prisoners were often locked in their cells for as many as 22 hours a day, with staff shortages sometimes denying them even basic outdoor exercise.
 10 
 The “Arthur” star, seen arriving at Southwark Crown Court in London yesterday, could be forced to share a prison cell with vermin that sneak in through “crumbling floors.” Getty Images 
 10 
 Russell Brand sits in the dock at Southwark Crown Court in London in a court artist sketch. Elizabeth Cook/PA via AP 
 Violence was another major concern.
 During the 2023-24 reporting period, there were 442 inmate-on-inmate assaults and 518 on staff. The prison also recorded 998 incidents of self-harm involving 302 men.
 There were also 10 deaths during the reporting period, six of which were described as “apparently self-inflicted.”
 The report further noted that over half of surveyed inmates found it easy to get illicit drugs, while the odor of cannabis was described as pervasive throughout the facility.
 The prison logged 344 drug finds along with 115 alcohol discoveries during the reporting period.

 If Brand’s family visits him behind bars, they will face Wandsworth’s strict security procedures — and his young son, born in 2023, will not be exempt.
 The prison allows a maximum of three visitors per inmate at a time. First-time visitors must have their fingerprints taken for the security system, and anyone entering the facility, including children, must undergo a “rub-down search.”
 Security dogs are also on site, meaning visitors may be subjected to searches by passive drug-detection teams.
 Wandsworth also enforces a strict dress code, warning visitors they could be turned away for wearing vests, low-cut tops, high-cut shorts or dresses and ripped jeans. 
 Clothing with offensive patterns or slogans is prohibited, while scarves, gloves, watches, sunglasses and hats must be removed before entry — aside from religious head coverings.
 10 
 Laura Brand holds hands with her husband, the recently incarcerated “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” star as they head inside Southwark Crown Court. Russell’s being held at a facility known for being overcrowded. AP Photo/Thomas Krych 
 10 
 In a screen grab from a video released by police, Russell Brand reads a statement during an interview. Brand’s visitors in prison will have to undergo strict security screening. Metropolitan Police/AFP via Getty Images 
 However, the prison does offer inmates a chance to prepare for their next act.
 Inmates can take part in educational and vocational training, with courses ranging from English, math and computer skills to barbering, catering, bicycle repair, gardening, construction and radio production.
 Other activities include yoga, mindfulness, parenting skills, embroidery and choir.
 Brand will also have opportunities to maintain contact with his family, should they wish to keep in touch.
 The prison holds monthly family days, allowing inmates extra time with their children in a more relaxed setting, as well as a homework club where fathers can help with schoolwork.
 Video calls, phone calls and emails are also available.
 10 
 Laura Brand will have the opportunity visit her husband in HMP Wandsworth–after undergoing strict security protocol. Russell Brand/Youtube 
 10 
 Brand and his wife, Laura, arrive at Southwark Crown Court in London on Oct. 12. Laura will have the chance to visit her husband in prison during monthly family days in addition to regular visits. Getty Images 
 Following a nearly two-year investigation launched after several women went public with allegations, Brand was charged in 2025 with one count of rape, one count of oral rape, two counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault.
 Brand pleaded not guilty and denied the allegations throughout his trial. 
 Following Thursday’s convictions , Kally Sahota, an attorney and director of Sahota & Sahota Solicitors, exclusively told Page Six that he expects Brand to be sentenced to “eight or nine years.”
 Brand’s sentencing is scheduled for Monday.
